```{r}
# ============================================================
# POLITICAL ATTITUDES:
# ROBUSTNESS TO IDEOLOGY AND PARTY IDENTIFICATION
#
# Purpose:
# Assess whether the previously observed relationships between
# employment quality, race, and political attitudes remain after
# controlling for ideology, party identification, and the
# demographic controls used elsewhere in the analysis.
#
# This script intentionally does NOT conduct model-fit comparisons.
# It focuses on descriptive coefficient estimates and significance.
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(MASS)
library(broom)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare ideology and party identification
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_political_controls <- jqi_political %>%
  mutate(

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Political ideology
    #
    # 1 = Extremely liberal
    # 2 = Liberal
    # 3 = Slightly liberal
    # 4 = Moderate
    # 5 = Slightly conservative
    # 6 = Conservative
    # 7 = Extremely conservative
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    polviews_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(polviews)),

    polviews_factor = case_when(
      polviews_num %in% 1:7 ~ polviews_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    polviews_factor = factor(
      polviews_factor,
      levels = 1:7,
      labels = c(
        "Extremely liberal",
        "Liberal",
        "Slightly liberal",
        "Moderate",
        "Slightly conservative",
        "Conservative",
        "Extremely conservative"
      )
    ),


    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Party identification
    #
    # 0 = Strong Democrat
    # 1 = Not very strong Democrat
    # 2 = Independent, close to Democrat
    # 3 = Independent
    # 4 = Independent, close to Republican
    # 5 = Not very strong Republican
    # 6 = Strong Republican
    # 7 = Other party
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    party_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(partyid)),

    party_factor = case_when(
      party_num %in% 0:7 ~ party_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    party_factor = factor(
      party_factor,
      levels = 0:7,
      labels = c(
        "Strong Democrat",
        "Not very strong Democrat",
        "Independent, close to Democrat",
        "Independent",
        "Independent, close to Republican",
        "Not very strong Republican",
        "Strong Republican",
        "Other party"
      )
    ),

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Race
    # White = reference
    # Black = comparison
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    race_group = case_when(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 1 ~ "White",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 2 ~ "Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    race_group = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c("White", "Black")
    ),

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Sex
    # Male = reference
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    sex_factor = case_when(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)) == 1 ~ "Male",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)) == 2 ~ "Female",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    sex_factor = factor(
      sex_factor,
      levels = c("Male", "Female")
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Verify coding
# ------------------------------------------------------------

table(
  jqi_political_controls$polviews_factor,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

table(
  jqi_political_controls$party_factor,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

table(
  jqi_political_controls$race_group,
  useNA = "ifany"
)


# ============================================================
# 3. FUNCTION: FULL POLITICAL ATTITUDE MODEL
# ============================================================

run_controlled_political_model <- function(data, outcome) {

  # Full model:
  #
  # Employment status
  # + subjective social class
  # + JQI components
  # + occupational prestige
  # + income
  # + demographics
  # + ideology
  # + party ID
  #
  # Race is included both as a main effect and in interactions
  # with each JQI component.

  formula_text <- paste0(
    outcome,
    " ~ ",
    "wrkstat_factor + ",
    "social_class_factor + ",
    "compensation * race_group + ",
    "benefits * race_group + ",
    "earnings_stability * race_group + ",
    "prestige + ",
    "log_realrinc + ",
    "age + ",
    "sex_factor + ",
    "educ + ",
    "polviews_factor + ",
    "party_factor"
  )

  model_formula <- as.formula(formula_text)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Complete-case sample for this outcome/model
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  model_vars <- all.vars(model_formula)

  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(model_vars)) %>%
    na.omit() %>%
    droplevels()

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Check that outcome has sufficient variation
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (length(unique(model_data[[outcome]])) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit ordered logit
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  model <- MASS::polr(
    model_formula,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract coefficients
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  results <- broom::tidy(
    model
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      outcome = outcome,
      n = nrow(model_data)
    )

  return(
    list(
      model = model,
      results = results,
      data = model_data
    )
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 4. RUN MODELS FOR ALL FIVE POLITICAL ATTITUDES
# ============================================================

political_outcomes <- c(
  "eqwlth",
  "getahead",
  "kidssol",
  "poleff11",
  "tax"
)

controlled_models <- setNames(
  lapply(
    political_outcomes,
    function(x) {
      run_controlled_political_model(
        jqi_political_controls,
        x
      )
    }
  ),
  political_outcomes
)


# ============================================================
# 5. COMBINE COEFFICIENT RESULTS
# ============================================================

controlled_results <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    controlled_models,
    function(x) {

      if (is.null(x)) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      x$results
    }
  )
)

controlled_results


# ============================================================
# 6. JQI COMPONENT RESULTS
#
# These are the coefficients we care about most.
# ============================================================

jqi_controlled_results <- controlled_results %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "compensation",
      "benefits",
      "earnings_stability"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    term
  )

jqi_controlled_results
jqi_controlled_results


# ============================================================
# 7. RACE MAIN EFFECTS
# ============================================================

race_controlled_results <- controlled_results %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "compensation",
      "benefits",
      "earnings_stability"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    term
  )


print(race_controlled_results)


# ============================================================
# 8. RACE × JQI INTERACTIONS
#
# These directly test whether the relationship between
# employment quality and political attitudes differs by race
# after accounting for ideology, party, and demographics.
# ============================================================

race_jqi_controlled_results <- controlled_results %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "compensation:race_groupBlack",
      "race_groupBlack:benefits",
      "race_groupBlack:earnings_stability"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    term
  )

print(race_jqi_controlled_results)
?racecen1

# ============================================================
# 9. IDEOLOGY COEFFICIENTS
#
# Useful for documenting that ideology is being held constant,
# but these are not the primary substantive results.
# ============================================================

ideology_results <- controlled_results %>%
  filter(
    grepl("^polviews_factor", term)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  )

ideology_results


# ============================================================
# 10. PARTY ID COEFFICIENTS
#
# Again, these are controls rather than the focus of the analysis.
# ============================================================

party_results <- controlled_results %>%
  filter(
    grepl("^party_factor", term)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  )

party_results


# ============================================================
# 11. FULL DEMOGRAPHIC / CONTROL RESULTS
# ============================================================

demographic_control_terms <- c(
  "race_groupBlack",
  "age",
  "sex_factorFemale",
  "education",
  "log_realrinc",
  "prestige"
)

demographic_results <- controlled_results %>%
  filter(
    term %in% demographic_control_terms
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    term
  )

demographic_results


# ============================================================
# 12. SAVE RESULTS
# ============================================================

write.csv(
  jqi_controlled_results,
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "political_attitudes_JQI_ideology_party_controls.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  race_controlled_results,
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "political_attitudes_race_ideology_party_controls.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  race_jqi_controlled_results,
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "political_attitudes_race_JQI_interactions_ideology_party_controls.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# 13. OPTIONAL: COMPACT SUMMARY TABLE
#
# This gives you the key coefficients in one table for easy
# comparison across the five political outcomes.
# ============================================================

jqi_summary_table <- controlled_results %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "compensation",
      "benefits",
      "earnings_stability",
      "race_groupBlack",
      "compensation:race_groupBlack",
      "race_groupBlack:benefits",
      "race_groupBlack:earnings_stability"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    term
  )

jqi_summary_table
```
